newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch minister urges cutting deficit below 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch minister urges cutting deficit below 2 pct.

text.p: Dutch Economics Minister Hans Wijers said on Monday the government must cut the official government deficit to below two percent of GDP by 1998.
He addressed a D-66 party meeting in Arnhem saying the deficit in 1998 must begin, "clearly with the figure one before the comma (decimal point)."
D-66 is part of the ruling coalition.

Wijers aims to tackle the deficit with what he has called the "Delta model", announced last week. The model calls for tax relief of 10 billion guilders and government investment of four billion guilders. The number of benefits claimants also must fall by between 25,000 and 50,000 a year.
Wijers has based his policy and forecasts on gross domestic product (GDP) growth of three percent per year.
The government's official definition of a deficit is not identical to the one specified by the European Union to meet the qualification for Economic and Monetary Union.
In September, the government forecast an official deficit of 2.8 percent for 1997, leading to a deficit for EMU purposes of 2.2 percent.
